newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Ericsson, steel lift Swedish shares to new high.
newsitem.headline: Ericsson, steel lift Swedish shares to new high.

text.p: Swedish shares rose to highs on Thursday, opening higher in line with the U.S. and boosted by blue-chip stocks Ericsson and Astra but the main focus of the day was the telecoms sector.
The general index closed 0.43 percent higher at 2,621.51, a record close, after shares worth 5.64 billion crowns changed hands.
"It is a very liquid market which is rising strongly in all sectors," one broker said.
"I think it can continue rising for the rest of the week with both the dollar and interest rates supporting this."
The telecoms sector was in focus with Finnish company Nokia posting its 1996 results. It reported a pre-tax profit before minorities of 3.90 billion Finnish markka against 4.93 billion a year ago.
Swedish rival Ericsson closed three crowns higher at 249 crowns.
Blue chip drugs group Astra gained one to 356.5 crowns.

Companies posting results included two steel companies. SSAB closed 3.5 crowns up at 118.5 after posting a 45 percent fall in profit after financial itens to 2.09 billion crowns. The market expected a profit of 1.98 billion.
Swedish-Anglo steel group Avesta Sheffield rose 1.5 to 76 crowns after announcing a pre-tax loss of 136 million crowns for the first nine months of 1996/97.

Engineering group Atlas Copco posted an eight percent rise in 1996 profit after financial items at 3.07 billion crowns with market expectations of a profit of 3.03 billion. It closed one crown lower at 173 crowns.
